approach: Root cause: an executable is written and run in the same process while a write handle (or a forked child that copied it) still holds the file. Earlier jobs guarded the last symptom. The tree is already mostly clean: every test stand-in goes through `athena_testkit::write_executable` except the `script` helper in the slot_exec.rs unit tests. This revision stays inside the brief's deliverable files (round 1 findings 3-8 flagged the new athena-data module and the edits to checks.rs, reading.rs, gh/transport.rs and run/mod.rs). Four parts. (1) Widen the scan in no_in_process_exec_writes.rs: add wrapper detection (a fn that hides a permission primitive, called from test code, same file or `pub` in another file; the athena-testkit helper is skipped when collecting wrappers) and a chmod-in-argument rule (`sh -c "chmod"`, `.arg("chmod")`, `.args([.. "chmod" ..])`, `Command::new(` split from `"chmod"`), with fixtures that fail on both and pass on the helper. (2) Convert the slot_exec.rs `script` helper to `write_executable` (executable) or `std::fs::write` (non-executable) and drop its EXEMPT entry. (3) Retry briefly on ETXTBSY where production code in the deliverable files runs a program that tests replace by a stand-in: make `retry_busy` in claude.rs `pub` (adding `retry_busy_with(attempts, pause, op)` for unit tests), use it for the real-cargo status in slot_exec.rs (athena-cli already depends on athena-agent), and give xtask its own std-only copy because xtask has no athena-agent edge and a Cargo.toml edit is outside the deliverables. (4) Record it: a CHANGELOG Fixed entry whose first sentence is the root cause, a D163 entry with the site table, and a D160→D163 link. toolconfig.rs, git/snapshot.rs and stand_in_stress.rs are deliverables but need no edit: their uses are non-stand-in production or the exempt control, and D163 lists them as such. No D08 path is touched. Run sites outside the deliverable files (checks.rs, reading.rs, gh/transport.rs, run/mod.rs) are named in D163 as not retried, with the follow-up proposed, and asked about in open_questions.

decisions.choice: Keep the change inside the listed deliverables. Retry sites are claude.rs (already), slot_exec.rs and xtask/src/main.rs; the other run sites are named in D163 as a proposed follow-up.

Every test stand-in is written through the helper, which removes the race at its origin; the retry is a second layer where the brief lists the file.

decisions.choice: Scan widening: (a) wrapper detection: a fn whose body holds a permission primitive or a chmod argument and none of 0o200, 0o222, set_readonly; any same-file fn counts, a `pub` or `pub(crate)` fn counts in every file; fns in crates/athena-testkit/src are skipped (the helper itself runs chmod in its child shell). A call in a test region is flagged `wrapper call`. (b) chmod-in-argument rule: a non-comment test-region line with the word `chmod` and one of `Command::new(`, `.arg(`, `.args(`, `"sh"`, `"bash"`, `-c`, unless it calls `write_executable(`; plus a bare `"chmod"` line after a line ending `Command::new(`. `violations(rel, text)` stays pure and delegates to `violations_with(rel, text, shared)`.
decisions.reason: These are the shapes the request names. The write-bit exclusion keeps the read-only toggles in pin.rs, core/snapshot.rs and git/snapshot.rs from becoming wrappers. Skipping the helper keeps its own chmod from flagging every caller.

risks.risk: The wrapper rule flags a legitimate test call (a read-only toggle, or a shared name used by an unrelated fn).
risks.mitigation: Fns that mention 0o200/0o222/set_readonly are not wrappers; cross-file wrappers must be pub or pub(crate); athena-testkit/src is skipped. A fixture pins the write-bit toggle as not flagged, and the real-tree test shows the result. A hit is fixed or given a documented EXEMPT entry, never silently loosened.

risks.risk: The chmod text rule misses a split-line form or flags a policy string.
risks.mitigation: It needs the word chmod plus a command-building marker on the same line (or the split Command::new( case) and ignores lines that call write_executable(. Fixtures cover a policy-style array and a script body that mentions chmod. D163's Tradeoff states the text-scan limits.

risks.risk: The retry masks a real fault or slows a failing run.
risks.mitigation: At most 20 attempts of 50 ms (about 1 s), only on ETXTBSY; the last error is returned unchanged; other errors are not retried. Unit tests pin the bound.

risks.risk: A retried spawn or status call re-uses a Command whose settings are consumed.
risks.mitigation: A std Command can be spawned again after a failed spawn and keeps its settings. The producer builds `let mut cmd` first and calls `retry_busy(|| cmd.status())` / `cmd.output()`, keeping the per-site error text unchanged; the compiler and the existing tests check it.

risks.risk: Leaving the athena-core run sites unretried keeps a small residual window if a test there writes a stand-in in-process.
risks.mitigation: The scan now forbids in-process stand-in writes everywhere in tests, the stress test measures 0 busy files through the helper, and D163 and the open question name the follow-up.

risks.risk: Wrong line number in the new link or a malformed entry fails backtest or DecisionEntries.
risks.mitigation: D163 is appended last so earlier lines do not shift; the producer reads the link line from Grep -n 'Amends D160' docs/decisions.md after the final edit and runs the backtest and mirrors tests.

risks.risk: The introspection record records/introspections/2026-11/20261106-104005-m047.json is not in the planner's copy, so its proposed_request was not checked.
risks.mitigation: The root cause and fix follow the request text and the code. The producer must not edit the record.
